segments.title: 第148章 未來女婿
segments.content:
Chapter 148: Future Son-in-law

They recorded until after three in the afternoon, then Li Luo went downstairs to the kitchen to cook.

Yan Zhusheng, claiming she could help, also pattered downstairs in her slippers and joined Li Luo in the kitchen.

This left Yuan Wanqing and Luo Fei alone in the recording studio.

"What do you think?" Yuan Wanqing turned the player back on, playing the song they had just recorded. She listened to the melody and lyrics before asking her best friend.

Luo Fei hummed softly along with the melody, a thoughtful expression appearing in her eyes. "How should I put it? It feels quite magical."

"What do you mean?"

"Because if you put these four songs in front of me all at once, I'd have a really hard time believing they were all written by the same person." Luo Fei smiled and explained.

"Purely from a melodic standpoint, it's still plausible. But look at the lyrics of these two songs, plus the previous 'Waiting for You After Class' and 'Annual Rings'."

"'Annual Rings' is a standard ancient-style song, and its lyrics read more like the emotional pain from a woman's perspective."

"Then 'Waiting for You After Class' is from a man's perspective, talking about the process and inner monologue of a boy silently crushing on and pursuing a girl. It has a very diary-like feel."

"Now with these two, one is 'Chaser of the Light,' with lyrics that are more like a poem. The imagery is rich and subtle, with all sorts of expressions half-veiled by metaphors, not at all as direct as 'Waiting for You After Class'."

"And the other song, 'Light,' is more of an inspirational, coming-of-age song, with a completely different narrative from the other three."

"So you mean," Yuan Wanqing frowned, "Li Luo didn't write these songs?"

"That's not it," Luo Fei said with a laugh. "Didn't you tell me his family is just an ordinary one? His parents run a breakfast shop. How could he possibly find a ghostwriter?"

"I can only say that geniuses really do exist in this world. He must be very skilled at songwriting."

"And judging by his demeanor and how he handles things, he's a very mature person. It's probably related to his family running a breakfast shop."

Yuan Wanqing nodded lightly. "Zhusheng mentioned to me that Li Luo's essay for the high school entrance exam in Chinese got a perfect score."

"But being able to write these four songs is much more impressive than getting a perfect score on an essay, in my opinion," Luo Fei said, shaking her head.

"The lyrics of 'Annual Rings' feel a bit like complaining about nothing, with many words forced just for the sake of rhyming. But when paired with a Xianxia drama, it works well enough."

"'Waiting for You After Class' is almost too direct. Every line is very colloquial, like a diary entry written offhand."

"But when it comes to 'Chaser of the Light'... the improvement from the previous two is honestly quite significant. The use of lyrical imagery isn't as rigid as in 'Annual Rings,' and the sentences aren't as direct as in 'Waiting for You After Class'."

"And in the song 'Light,' you can even see a bit of his reflections on life."

"Especially this line."

"That I have to turn on my own"

"To be able to find the light"

"The sun has always been in that place"

Luo Fei sang the lines aloud, clearly quite fond of this part of the melody and lyrics, then said:

"If an adult wrote these lines, I'd think it's quite normal. But for them to come from a sixteen-year-old, it shows he really does spend time thinking about things."

After hearing her out, Yuan Wanqing couldn't help but smile. "It sounds like you really admire him?"

"What else?" Luo Fei hummed. "What were we doing when we were fifteen or sixteen? But Li Luo has already sold a song and earned tens of thousands of yuan."

"Then do you think..." Yuan Wanqing was tempted. She looked at the lyric book on the table and mused in a low voice, "How would these two songs do in the current market?"

"That's hard to say," Luo Fei said, shaking her head. "I can only evaluate the song based on its melody and lyrics. But nowadays, whether a song can become a hit doesn't just depend on that."

"But I don't want to just rely on the company to solicit songs anymore," Yuan Wanqing said, pursing her lips.

"You just released an album. You can't release another one so soon."

"I know," Yuan Wanqing nodded. "That's why I'm just asking for your opinion first. Even if I were to release a new album, I'd definitely need to prepare for a year. But it's good to get your hands on good songs early."

"Hmm..." Luo Fei thought for a moment. With Li Luo's recorded voice playing in her ears, she fell into deep thought, unsure of what advice to give. In the end, she could only joke, "Why don't you just ask Li Luo if he can write a few more for you?"

Yuan Wanqing raised a hand to her forehead. "That's a bit shameless of you to say."

"You never know," Luo Fei giggled. "Look at Li Luo, it's only been two or three months, right? And he's already produced four songs."

"If you give him a year to prepare, ten songs for an album would be a piece of cake for him, wouldn't it?"

"Besides, in another five or six years, he might just be your son-in-law."

At that last sentence, Yuan Wanqing shot her a glare. "What are you talking about? They're still just kids. You're the one thinking so far ahead."

"I've never seen Zhusheng so clingy with a boy before," Luo Fei said with a pout. "She even has to stay with him while he's cooking. I just wonder if Zhusheng herself has realized it."

"You're talking a little too much today."

"Haha, I'll stop, I'll stop. If I provoke you any further, I'm afraid you'll give him the cold shoulder later."

Yuan Wanqing sighed. "You only say this to me in private. Don't say anything rash during dinner later. They're still students, so their studies should be the priority."

"Especially about the new album, don't you dare mention it to Li Luo, lest he gets his hopes up and it affects his studies."

"His grades are excellent at school right now. If his grades slip because of me, I wouldn't know how to explain it to his parents."

"I know, I know," Luo Fei waved her hand. "I was just teasing you. I'm not that tactless."

"But..." Yuan Wanqing looked down in thought, then said, "We can go ahead and acquire these two songs from Li Luo. What do you think?"

"It's up to you," Luo Fei said. "If it weren't for that previous song 'Waiting for You After Class' being so unsuitable for your style, I would have highly recommended it too."

"Then it's settled."

Around four-thirty in the afternoon, Li Luo finished making four small dishes and carried them to the dining table with Yan Zhusheng.

Yan Zhusheng called the two aunties downstairs for dinner, and Li Luo explained, "I didn't know you were coming beforehand, so I didn't buy a lot of groceries."

"It's fine," Yuan Wanqing shook her head and sat down at the table. "You were supposed to be the guest, coming to our home to hang out. Making you cook is already embarrassing enough."

"It smells so good," Luo Fei sat down next to her and leaned in for a sniff. "I didn't believe it when Zhusheng told me, but looking at this, it might really be better than what our private cook makes."

Yan Zhusheng nodded, then eagerly picked up her chopsticks, put a slice of eel into her mouth, and her eyes instantly narrowed in comfort.

After Yuan Wanqing and Luo Fei tasted the food, they too were full of praise, surprised that Li Luo's cooking skills were so good.

Normally, neither of them ate much for dinner. After all, as they got older, their metabolism slowed down, and eating less was necessary to maintain their figures.

But after eating the meal Li Luo prepared, both of them finished a large bowl of rice each, eating until they were stuffed.

It was only after they were full that Yuan Wanqing remembered about the two songs.

So she wiped her mouth, looked at Li Luo sitting across from her, and after some thought, said to him, "Li Luo, Auntie wants to discuss something with you."

A little after five in the evening, Li Luo was sitting in Yuan Wanqing's MPV, being driven back to Bihai Lanting by her driver.

Because he had promised Ying Chanxi he would be back for dinner in the evening, he had purposely started cooking early at Yan Zhusheng's house so he could make it home by five-thirty.

He hadn't expected that what was originally just a plan to record the songs and then ask Yan Zhusheng to send them to her mother's company to see if anyone was interested.

Ended up with him selling the songs smoothly just by meeting Yuan Wanqing...

Of course, what he sold was still only partial copyright for the songs.

But unlike with "Annual Rings," this time the sale was mainly related to the album and performance rights.

With "Annual Rings" as a precedent, and because they were acquaintances, Yuan Wanqing didn't try to haggle. She offered the standard market price and didn't try to pull any tricks just because he was a kid.

In particular, the deal they negotiated was a one-time copyright fee plus a royalty-sharing model. This meant that if these two songs were included in Yuan Wanqing's album in the future.

Li Luo would be able to get a share of the album's future profits.

Of course, album profits were on a steep decline these days, but it was still a gesture of sincerity from Yuan Wanqing.

Being treated as an equal by a fifteen or sixteen-year-old was already quite good for Li Luo.

He just didn't expect that out of four songs, it was Jay Chou's song that became the only one he couldn't sell...

But then he remembered that Jay Chou had his share of rejections when he was young, and Li Luo felt more at ease.

For most people, it was still too difficult to judge whether a song would be a hit before it was even released.

With these thoughts, the MPV steadily delivered him to the entrance of his residential complex.

After thanking the driver, Li Luo pushed open the door, got out, and walked into the complex, quickly returning to apartment 1502.

As soon as he opened the door, Li Luo saw three girls sitting in the living room.

Probably because Lin Xiuhong was busy in the kitchen, Xu Youyu was, for once, not sprawled on the sofa but sitting up properly.

Qiao Xinyan was sitting on the other side of the sofa, quietly watching the TV playing in the living room.

Ying Chanxi sat in the very middle, hugging the Pikachu plushie. It seemed she really liked the gift from Yan Zhusheng.

"Why are you back so late?" Ying Chanxi asked when she saw Li Luo. "A little later and Auntie Lin would have finished cooking."

"I was at someone's house borrowing their recording studio, after all," Li Luo said while changing his shoes. "So I made them a meal as thanks, and then I rushed back."

Hearing this, Ying Chanxi immediately squeezed the Pikachu's head.

"Then go get me a Xiao Buding."

"Alright, alright, Young Miss Ying," Li Luo was given an order as soon as he put on his slippers. He walked into the kitchen and took a Xiao Buding out of the freezer.

The next second, Lin Xiuhong's voice came from the kitchen: "You brat, it's almost time for dinner and you're eating a Xiao Buding? Put it back."

"Ying Chanxi wants it."

"Oh... then why haven't you taken it to her yet?"

Li Luo: "...You're really her own mother, huh."

"What are you dawdling for? Take it to Xixi, then hurry back and lend a hand."

(End of this chapter)
